messages:
Sam: FYI - noticed a regression after the kernel-autotune rollout to prod-gpu pools. Long contexts (>=1024) have ~2x decode latency on g5. Autotuner switched a bunch of models from `attn-ptx` -> `fused-attn-v2` during prefill profiling.

Sam: Quick numbers from canary (same model, same batch=1):
```
seq | prefill_ms | decode_ms | kernel pick (prefill/decode)
32  | 85         | 12        | fused-attn-v2 / attn-ptx
128 | 120        | 30        | fused-attn-v2 / attn-ptx
1024| 400        | 250       | fused-attn-v2 / fused-attn-v2
2048| 920        | 480       | fused-attn-v2 / attn-ptx
```
These look odd: for 2048 decode ms jumped and kernel pick flipped back to `attn-ptx` for decode, even though prefill stuck with fused.

Diego: Hmm. Do you have an `nsys` or kernel timeline? Could be KV-cache memory pattern + kernel selection mismatch between prefill and decode paths.

Sam: Pasting the hot kernel snippet from `nsys` (trimmed):
```
Kernel: fused_attn_v2_forward  time: 380ms  blocks: 120  SM eff: 78%
Kernel: attn_ptx_forward      time: 460ms  blocks: 96   SM eff: 62%
KV cache copy:               time: 45ms   (additional memcpy during decode for 2nd layer)
```
But the scheduler chose `attn-ptx` during decode on 2048 which correlates to the 480ms decode.

Priya: That memcpy during decode sounds like a KV cache path mismatch. Are we using different block/packing assumptions for prefill vs decode? We historically optimized prefill for contiguous KV writes and decode for streaming reads. If the kernel autotuner is only trained on prefill traces it may prefer kernels that look good for the prefill memory layout but perform worse when decode does repeated small reads.

Alex: Good call. Two quick hypotheses: 1) autotune sampling bias (prefill-heavy data) -> picks kernels not representative of decode, 2) our kernel selection table doesn't encode path-specific constraints (prefill vs decode) or sequence-length hysteresis, so we flip mid-request.

Sam: Repro steps I ran: `python tools/rperf.py --model m7b --seq 2048 --profile --warm 2 --runs 5`
We see decode variance spike when KV-cache warmed but with different alignment. Cold start decode looks fine. Warmed KV shows regressions.

Diego: Can you dump the selected kernel metadata for prefill vs decode for a few layers? I want to see whether the autotuner key includes `path=prefill` vs `path=decode`. If it doesn't, that's a bug.

Sam: Dumped. Example layer 3: `key={arch:amX, seq:2048, batch:1, path:prefill}` -> `fused-attn-v2`. `key={arch:amX, seq:2048, batch:1, path:decode}` -> `attn-ptx`.

Priya: That's the problem. We currently only persisted per-(seq,batch,arch) and the path got encoded heuristically; autotuner DB uses sampling weight but not explicit path dimension. Need to store `path` and maybe `kv_alignment` flags.

Alex: Short-term mitigation: add a path-aware override so decode always prefers kernels validated on streaming reads for seq>512. Also add hysteresis when switching picks between prefill/decode inside a single request: require N consecutive frames to prefer new kernel. That should avoid per-request flips.

perf-bot: [alert] Canary alert: decode P50 for seq>=1024 increased by 85% in pool prod-gpu-1 at 2026-03-16T14:12:10Z. Ticket created: RINF-4531.

Sam: Long-term: we should retrain or re-run autotune with explicit path sampling (prefill/decode), include KV cache alignment patterns, and capture memcpy patterns (copy-on-read vs in-place). Also consider separate kernel catalogs: one for prefill-many-writes and one for decode-streaming-reads.

Diego: I'll do a focused autotune run that samples 60% decode traces, 40% prefill. Also will add flags to the kernel metadata: `kv_write_pattern` and `kv_read_granularity`.

Priya: I can add instrumentation to the runtime to expose KV copy reasons (alignment/stride/misalignment) and then add that to telemetry samples so autotuner can learn it. Minimal change: tag traces with `kv_copy=true/false` and `copy_bytes`.

Alex: Owners & next steps:
- Diego: run path-balanced autotune and produce a new kernel table (due EOD tomorrow)
- Priya: runtime telemetry change to emit `kv_copy` tags (PR by EOD today)
- Sam: run canary with new table on canary pool and attach `nsys` traces (tomorrow morning)

Sam: One more note: we should not only bucket by sequence length, but also by `active_kv_bytes` (how much KV is addressed per token). Two seq-2048 traces with different addressed token windows can behave very differently.

Diego: Agreed. Adding `active_kv_bytes` to autotune key.

Alex: Also let's add a simple unit test in our autotune infra: run a micro-benchmark that simulates streaming decode access patterns and ensure chosen kernels meet a threshold. If a kernel fails for streaming, mark it as incompatible for decode path.

Sam: Cool. I'll post follow-ups after I run the canary. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Priya: Nice catch. We'll iterate.
